title: Set a lens and screen on an optical bench for a sharp, same-size image
instruction: Set up the converging lens (focal length 100 mm) and the white screen on the optical bench so that a sharp image of the lamp's arrow, the same size as the arrow, falls on the screen. Leave both standing upright on the bench, square across it and on its centre line, the screen's white face toward the lamp.
context: Physics teachers and school science technicians set up ray-optics demonstrations and class practicals on an optical bench: a lamp box with an arrow slide as the object, a converging lens in a holder and a white screen, each on a rider. The result taught at GCSE and A level and in introductory college physics: an object at twice the focal length (2F) gives a real, inverted image of the same size at 2F on the far side, so the screen stands 4f from the object, the shortest distance at which a lens forms a real image on a screen. A screen nearer than 4f can never be focused, wherever the lens goes, and a lens inside its focal length gives no image on the screen at all. Here the lens (f = 100 mm) starts 50 mm from the arrow and the screen 280 mm, so both must move: the lens to 200 mm, the screen to 400 mm, each left standing upright and square across the bench.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. Distances along the bench are along y, from the object plane (the face of the arrow slide) toward -y. (1) Optical bench: a fixed grey anodised aluminium strip, 60 mm wide (x), 560 mm long and 6 mm tall, centred on x 30.0 cm, from y +26.0 to -30.0 cm. (2) Lamp box: fixed, black steel, 60 mm (x) by 59 mm (y) and 76 mm tall, standing on the bench's left end (x 27.0 to 33.0 cm, y +20.1 to +26.0 cm). On its -y face a white card slide 40 x 40 mm, 1 mm thick, centred on x 30.0 cm and 45 mm above the bench top; its face, at y +20.0 cm, is the object plane. On the slide a black printed upward arrow 30 mm tall (30 to 60 mm above the bench top): a shaft 4 mm wide and a head 12 mm wide. The lamp is not lit in the simulation. (3) Scale: 11 black vinyl-tape ticks on the table beside the bench's -x side (2 mm wide, 1 mm tall, ending 5 mm from the bench), one every 50 mm from the object plane, 0 to 500 mm (y +20.0 to -30.0 cm); those at every 100 mm are 16 mm long, the others 10 mm. (4) Lens in its holder, loose, 80 g, focal length 100 mm (marked): a black plastic rider 50 mm (x) by 40 mm (y) and 12 mm tall; on it a dark grey plastic holder frame 50 mm wide, 22 mm thick (y) and 80 mm tall (12 to 92 mm above the rider's underside), with a 38 x 38 mm window (26 to 64 mm up) holding the glass lens, shown as a pale blue block filling the window, 23 mm thick (0.5 mm proud of each face); the lens's centre, 45 mm up, is level with the arrow's. It stands on the bench centred on x 30.0 cm, its centre at y +15.0 cm (50 mm from the arrow), square across the bench. (5) Screen, loose, 90 g: a black plastic rider 60 mm (x) by 40 mm (y) and 12 mm tall; on it a rigid foam board 100 mm wide, 22 mm thick and 100 mm tall (12 to 112 mm up), painted white on its lamp side (+y), with a 1 mm black plastic back, the white face 11 mm from the rider's centre. It stands on the bench centred on x 30.0 cm, square across it, its white face toward the lamp at y -8.0 cm (280 mm from the arrow). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from where the lens and the screen stand at the last step. An element's centre is the middle of its rider's underside. u is the distance along the bench (in y) from the object plane to the lens's centre (45 mm up); d is from the object plane to the screen's white face at the same height; v = d - u, the lens to the screen. An element counts when it is at rest (no corner of its rider and not its top moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s), resting on the bench (its centre over the bench top, the lowest corner of its rider's underside within 3 mm of the bench top), upright (tilted 5 degrees or less), square across the bench seen from above (within 5 degrees; the lens either way round, the screen with its white face toward the lamp) and centred (its centre within 8 mm of the bench's centre line, x 30.0 cm). The image is sharp when both elements count, u is over f = 100 mm, v is over 0, and v is within 10 mm of the image distance the lens law gives for the lens's actual position, v* = f u / (u - f) (from 1/u + 1/v = 1/f). Score 0 if the lens or the screen is tipped (tilted more than 10 degrees: leaning over, lying down or upside down) or off the bench (its centre more than 3 mm below the bench top: on the table). Otherwise: 1.0 if the image is sharp and the same size as the arrow (magnification v / u from 0.9 to 1.1); 0.5 if it is sharp at any other size; 0.25 if it is not sharp but one counting element is at its same-size mark (the lens 190 to 210 mm from the arrow, or the screen's face 390 to 410 mm); otherwise 0. Possible scores 0, 0.25, 0.5 and 1.0; every outcome maps to exactly one. Examples: the start (lens 50 mm, screen 280 mm) 0, since a lens inside its focal length gives no real image and no lens position focuses a screen nearer than 4f = 400 mm; lens 200 and screen 400 mm 1.0 (with each anywhere within 6 mm of its mark, all 169 combinations at 1 mm steps score 1.0); lens 150 and screen 450 mm (sharp, twice the size) 0.5; lens 300 and screen 450 mm (sharp, half the size) 0.5; lens at 200 mm with the screen left at 280 mm 0.25; screen at 400 mm with the lens left at 50 mm 0.25; lens 200 and screen 370 mm (blurred) 0.25; lens 120 and screen 300 mm 0. A screen turned round (white face away from the lamp), an element held above the bench, leaning more than 5 degrees or more than 8 mm off the centre line does not count. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 2.5 s. In a real trial the score comes from measurements with the marked f, not from looking at the image (the lamp may stay off): a rule along the bench (or the ticks in a top photo) gives u and d, a set square the tilt and squareness, a 3 mm feeler gauge the gap under a rider.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction. No light is simulated: the scorer applies the thin-lens law with the marked f = 100 mm to the two elements' poses. The lens is a block filling the holder's window (a real one is a 38 mm biconvex lens a few mm thick). The riders stand free on a flat bench, not on a rail. Each element is one rigid body of boxes. The scorer sees only the lens and the screen, so an element held still on the bench counts.
reset_notes: Stand the lens back on the bench with its centre at y +15.0 cm (50 mm from the arrow) and the screen with its white face toward the lamp at y -8.0 cm (280 mm from the arrow), both centred on x 30.0 cm and square across the bench. The bench, lamp box and scale are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
